root.name: Scandinavian Defense: Schiller-Pytel Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qd6 4. d4 c6

overview: Black has played the queen to d6 and supports it with ...c6, then develops ...Nf6, ...Bf5 and ...e6 for a compact Caro-Kann-like set-up. The input's most played lines go 4...Nf6 5.Bc4 c6 6.Nge2 Bf5 7.Bf4 Qb4, with the queen hopping to b4 to hit b2. White has a lead in development and more space; Black aims for a solid structure and ...e6 and ...Nbd7 with equal chances.

white_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with Bc4, Nge2 and Bf4 and keep the lead in development.
Exploit the queen's position with Nb5 or tactics on the d-file.

black_ideas.idea: Build a Caro-Kann-like structure with ...c6, ...Bf5 and ...e6 and develop ...Nbd7.
Harass b2 with the queen on b4 and gain time.

typical_structures.structure: White d4 centre against Black c6 and e6 pawns with the queen and light bishop active on the queenside and the bishop out on f5.

character.notes: Black keeps a compact, hard-to-attack structure although the queen moves cost time and some tactics exist.

gambit.notes: The d5 pawn is recaptured by the queen at once.

structure.notes: The Scandinavian asymmetry with a half-open d-file is semi-open.

approach.notes: Played by a number of strong players as a branch of the Scandinavian, so standard.

level.notes: Plans are clear, the main risk is tempo loss with the queen, little memory needed.

character.reason: Black builds a Caro-Kann-like compact structure that is hard to break down.

gambit.reason: The pawn on d5 is recaptured at once.

structure.reason: Asymmetric centre with a half-open d-file, as in all Scandinavian lines.

approach.reason: A respectable branch of the Scandinavian.

plans.reason: Black's queen moves early while White develops with tempo.
